subject: Inter-Category alignment of geom_text w/ position_jitter?

messages.author: 1d86582bcffce052
messages.subject: Inter-Category alignment of geom_text w/ position_jitter?
parts:
In the following example:

    df <- data.frame(cat = rep(c("cat1","cat2"), 100), val = rep(c(5,10), 100))
    ggplot(df, aes(x = val, y = cat)) +
        geom_jitter(position = position_jitter(width = 0)) +
        geom_text(aes(y = cat, x = val, label = cat))

The text labels appear centered (vertically) within the region created by geom_jitter.  Is there a way to cause the text to be aligned to either the top or bottom of the region instead? 

I can use trial-and-error to make "vjust" work with unsupported/non-standard values but that is not really a viable solution. 

My other thought is to figure out which integer value each category takes on.  Within the y-scale the regions created by position_jitter appear to be the integer factor +/- 0.50 and so I can use an explicit y-position instead of a factor reference to position absolutely.

I was hoping to use "position = position_dodge(height = -0.50)" but since there is only a single text no "dodging" is required.  I guess a "position_offset(height = -0.50)" would be useful to force the dodging to occur regardless of whether over-plotting exists.

Thank!

David J

Agreed.

>
> My other thought is to figure out which integer value each category takes
> on. Within the y-scale the regions created by position_jitter appear to be
> the integer factor +/- 0.50 and so I can use an explicit y-position instead
> of a factor reference to position absolutely.

I think this is reasonable, especially since you can explicitly set
the amount of jitter. Here is my go at it.

>
> I was hoping to use "position = position_dodge(height = -0.50)" but since
> there is only a single text no "dodging" is required.

There is no dodging because there is no group, not because there is a
single text. In fact you are plotting the same text over the top of
itself, which among other things makes the text look fuzzy. To see
what I mean, try

ggplot(df, aes(x = val, y = cat)) +
geom_jitter(position = position_jitter(width = 0)) +

geom_text(aes(y = cat, x = val, label = cat),
position=position_jitter(width=0))

I guess a
> "position_offset(height = -0.50)" would be useful to force the dodging to
> occur regardless of whether over-plotting exists.

If you want to offset by -.5, just do aes(y=yvar-.5). No need for a
special function for this.

Best,
Ista

ggplot(df, aes(x = val, y = cat)) +

geom_jitter(position = position_jitter(width = 0, height=h.jitter)) +
with(df, annotate(geom="text",
y = as.numeric(unique(cat))+h.jitter,
x = unique(val),
label = unique(cat)))
